Aonami 02

Step-free guide

ForKinjo-futo

ElevatorエレベーターOne lift, every station

Every station on the Aonami Line has one lift — a single, station-to-street lift, not several to choose between. Of the six operators at Nagoya, this is the simplest one to plan.

AThe lift
Station-to-street. Platform edge gates here too, and full platform doors at Kinjo-futo.
Boarding
The step and gap between the platform and the train floor are kept small.
On the train
A wheelchair space in the leading car. A chime sounds before the doors close.

Accessible toilet車椅子トイレOne, every station

Every station on the line has one barrier-free toilet.

AThe toilet
Spoken announcements and chimes mark the gates, the stairs and the toilet.
Exact position
Not published in text for Nagoya. Illustrated once we have walked it.

Entrances & exits出入口1F, far west end

Aonami Line Nagoya is on the ground floor, past the 太閤通南口 · Taikodori South Entrance — the furthest corner of the station from Sakuradori.

From JR
A connecting gate (連絡改札) takes you straight through, so you do not have to leave the building.
The gate itself
Wide ticket gates and ticket machines you can use seated.
Finding your way
Braille fare table and tactile paving throughout.
Coin lockers
1F, between the restrooms and the elevator, inside the ticket gates.

Help & information案内No need to book

Tell the station staff on the day you travel. There is no booking system.

One caveat
If staff are busy elsewhere you may have to wait a little.
Discounts
A fare discount applies to disabled passengers and one carer.

Source · Aonami Line barrier-free information (aonamiline.co.jp/guidance/accessibility); Nagoya Station Map (meieki.com), 1F sheet. Checked September 2026.
